input.quote: Termination by Sanofi for Convenience. Sanofi may terminate this Agreement (A) in its entirety by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed or (B) on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty or minimum-fee-on-termination concept payable by us. Searches for "liquidated damages" and "penalty" return nothing; Article IX imposes only ordinary consideration (upfront, milestone, royalty, profit/loss share) plus late-payment interest at LIBOR + margin capped at the legal maximum (§9.6), which the rule expressly treats as not a penalty. Termination for convenience under §12.2(a)(i) requires only notice — no break fee or minimum spend — and the termination consequences in §12.3(c) are reversion/transition obligations with post-termination royalties running from RevMed to us (§12.3(c)(ii)C), i.e., in our favour. The elective buy-in payment in §5.6(b)B is priced consideration for using RevMed study data, not a penalty. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages). Noted only: §12.6 preserves all other remedies for both parties, but that is a mutual general-remedies statement rather than a stipulated damages amount.
